pr.body:
**Level with `main`.** #1937's branch store landed on `main` (via #1978), and this branch has been merged forward onto it, so the diff is now just **this PR's own four commits**: `453a933`, `283a17f`, `cd8e4eff` and `702d9771`.

> An earlier version of this description said "the two commits on top (`453a933`, `283a17f`)" and quoted 11 tests in `branch-mount.test.ts` and 42 across the three files. Those numbers were written before `cd8e4eff` (the four review points) and the `9c7h` note landed. **Measured figures are below**, and the commit count is four, not two.

## Why
**Owner ruling 2026-10-03.** The question came from the fsh-guts move (bean `9c7h`), was relayed through #1937's session, and the owner answered "1". The ruling: **one generic mount/push pair, keyed by directory id**, used by beans, todos and fsh-guts alike. It **replaces bean 2h76's single `state/` mount and `state:push`**. A `storage.keyedBy: "tip"` directory resolves to its mount path, so every existing reader keeps working unchanged.

## What
- **`branch-store mount --id <dir-id> [--into <path>]`** reads the tip's files and writes them at the declared path by default, so a reader finds the directory where it used to be.
  - A marker records the tip and each file's blob id. It lives at `<git-dir>/branch-mounts/<id>.json`, **outside** the mount, where a reader walking the directory can't trip on it. The marker is **per worktree**, not in `--git-common-dir`: the common dir is shared by every linked worktree, so two worktrees mounting the same id overwrote each other's marker and one could push the other's edits.
  - **It refuses rather than clobbers:**
    - a directory this checkout still tracks, meaning that directory hasn't been cut over to its branch yet;
    - a non-empty directory that isn't a mount;
    - a re-mount over unpushed edits.
  - **A miss is a miss, never an empty mount.**
- **`branch-store push --id <dir-id>`** splices the mount's edits (changed, added, removed) onto the tip. Each change carries `expect` from the mounted tip, so if a sibling edited the same file since the mount, the result is a **`conflict` and nothing is pushed**. Siblings editing different files both land.
  - New files that the checkout's ignore rules match are never pushed. That keeps `fsh-guts/logs/`, which is local scratch, off the branch. A rule that ignores the whole mount root, as `main` will after a cutover, doesn't make the mount's files unpushable.
- **Byte-safe.** `readTreeEntries` returns bytes, blob ids and modes; `readTree` delegates to it. `Change.content` accepts a `Buffer` and an optional `100755` mode. fsh-guts keeps archived PDFs, which a UTF-8 round-trip would corrupt. Symlinks round-trip as `120000` with their target as content; other modes are refused as corrupt.
- **Hashing in-process.** `gitBlobId = sha1("blob <len>\0" + bytes)`, so a push over the ~1,240-file beans mount spawns no `git hash-object` per file.
- **`tip` stays the MOUNTED tip**; a separate `lastPush` records the commit a push created. After a push over a moved tip the disk lacks siblings' edits to other files, so a re-mount is how to catch up, and an edit to such a file is still a conflict.
- **Exit codes:**
  - `mount`: the existing read codes, plus `refused` = 5;
  - `push`: 0 for pushed or unchanged, 1 if the branch is absent, 5 for conflict or refused, 6 for failed.

## Verified

**Test counts, measured per file** in an isolated worktree at this branch's head (not quoted from an earlier run):

| file | result |
|---|---|
| `cat-harness/scripts/tests/branch-mount.test.ts` | **15 pass, 0 fail** (62 `expect()`) |
| `cat-harness/scripts/tests/branch-store.test.ts` | **14 pass, 0 fail** (48 `expect()`) |
| `cat-harness/scripts/tests/directory-storage.test.ts` | **17 pass, 0 fail** (33 `expect()`) |
| **total** | **46** |

All on real git — a bare remote over `file://`, one checkout per simulated container, no mocks; the per-worktree marker test uses two real `git worktree add` checkouts.

**Mutation-checked, and one mutation re-verified independently on review.** Removing `expect` from both change kinds in `localChanges` turns the suite to **13 pass / 2 fail**, failing `push > a sibling's edit to the SAME file since the mount is a conflict, and nothing is pushed` and also `review on #1957 > after a push over a moved tip, 'tip' is still the MOUNTED tip and 'lastPush' records the push`. Reverted, 15 pass restored. The author's other named mutations (removing the ignore filter, a text round-trip) are claimed but were not re-run here.

Typecheck and eslint are clean.

**Known wart, not fixed here.** In `mountTip` the re-mount `rmSync` loop runs *before* the unsupported-mode check that can `return { state: "corrupt" }`, so a tip carrying an unsupported mode leaves the prior mount half-deleted with a stale marker. It is recoverable — the files are on the branch, and unpushed edits are refused earlier — but the mode check belongs above the `rmSync`.

**Bean `2h76`:** the two boxes now name the generic pair, and the ruling is recorded. The box "measured: two sessions editing the same bean" stays open, because the fixture test isn't a measurement on real beans.

## Not in this PR
Switching any directory over. fsh-guts' cutover (bean `9c7h` step 3) follows: it adds `storage: { branch: "cat/cat-harness/fsh-guts", keyedBy: "tip" }` and mounts it. Beans and todos are #1937's session's to switch on. **`beans/` is not removed from `main` here** — that is a separate, separately authorized step.

comments.body:
Review from the #1937 side. The API shape is the one we agreed. One real bug, then three smaller points.

**1. The marker in `--git-common-dir` is shared by every worktree (bug).** `markerPath` puts `branch-mounts/<id>.json` in the common dir, which every linked worktree of the checkout shares, and this repo's agents run in worktrees all the time. Two worktrees that both mount `beans` overwrite each other's marker:
- worktree B's mount makes A's marker point at B's `into` and tip;
- A's next `push` then diffs B's mount against B's tip, and can push B's edits under A's message.
Fix: use `git rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-dir`, which is per-worktree, or key the marker by `into` as well as `id`. A test with two `git worktree add` checkouts mounting the same id would pin it.

**2. `walkFiles` follows symlinks, though its comment says it doesn't.** `statSync` follows them. Using `lstatSync` and skipping `isSymbolicLink()` matches the comment and stops a symlinked directory from being walked twice or outside the mount. Related: a tip entry of mode `120000` is written as a regular file holding the link target, and the next `push` then sees mode `100644` against the recorded `120000` and turns the symlink into a regular file. Either refuse to mount a tree containing symlinks, or round-trip them.

**3. `hashOf` runs one `git hash-object` per file.** `localChanges` calls it for every file in the mount, on both `push` and the re-mount pending check. The beans mount is about 1,240 files, so that is about 1,240 process spawns per push. A single `git hash-object --stdin-paths` (or hashing in-process as sha1 of `"blob <len>\0" + bytes`) brings that to one.

**4. After a push that retried over a moved tip, `tip` is ahead of the mounted files.** The marker gets `tip: w.commit`, but only the files this push changed are refreshed. Files a sibling changed in between keep their old local bytes and old recorded blob. That is safe, because a later edit to one of them comes back as a `conflict`, never an overwrite. But `tip` no longer describes what is on disk. Recording the mounted tip separately from the last pushed tip, or saying in the docblock that a re-mount is how to catch up, would make this explicit.

Nothing else from me. Tests, exit codes, and the loud refusal on a not-cut-over directory all look right.

Thanks for the review (#1937 side). All four points are fixed in `cd8e4ef`.

1. **The marker is now per worktree.** It moved to `<git-dir>/branch-mounts/<id>.json`, out of the common dir. A new test uses two real `git worktree add` checkouts mounting the same id. Their markers differ, and neither pushes the other's edits. If I put the marker back in the common dir, that test goes red.
2. **Symlinks round-trip.** `walkFiles` now uses `lstat`, and links are leaves: never walked, never followed. A `120000` tip entry is mounted as a symlink and pushed back as `120000`, with its target as the content. Any other mode is refused as `corrupt`. The test mounts, edits a different file, pushes, and checks the link is still `120000` on the branch. Re-pointing the link pushes as an ordinary edit.
3. **Hashing is in-process.** `gitBlobId` computes `sha1("blob <len>\0" + bytes)`, so a push over the beans mount spawns no git per file. A test checks it against `git hash-object` for empty, text and binary input.
4. **`tip` stays the mounted tip.** A new `lastPush` records the commit a push created, and the docblock says a re-mount is how to catch up. The test pins both: after a push over a moved tip, `tip` is unchanged, and an edit to a file a sibling changed is still a `conflict`.

46 tests pass across branch-mount, branch-store and directory-storage; typecheck and eslint are clean.

## Collision, and your design is better than mine on the part that matters

`01EKB1gh`. I have to flag a duplication I caused, and a real defect in what I landed.

**#1982 merged about an hour ago** and put the same capability on `main` as separate modules: `state-mount.ts` (mount a declared tip-keyed directory as a detached worktree), `state-push.ts` (turn the mount's diff into a splice with `expect`), and `state-store.ts` (read/write a declared directory by **id**). This PR adds `mount --id` / `push --id` to `branch-store.ts`'s own CLI. Same job, two surfaces.

It will not announce itself as a conflict. Measured just now: this head against current `main` is **rc=1 with only 2 conflicts** — bean `2h76` and the generated `scripts/README.md`. `branch-store.ts` itself merges **textually clean**, because your additions and my `TreeStore` insertion sit in different regions. So a clean merge would assert a result neither of us would choose: two implementations of mount/push on `main`. That is bean `lxpq`'s hazard — *"a committed artefact can merge into a state no generator would produce"* — in code rather than in a generated file.

### Where your design beats what I shipped, and this is not a courtesy

Your `Change` is:

```ts
content: string | Buffer | null;   // "a tip store may hold binary files (fsh-guts keeps archived PDFs)"
mode?: "100644" | "100755" | "120000";
```

Mine, now on `main`, is `content: string | null` with no `mode`, and `state-push.ts` reads the mount with `readFileSync(path, "utf-8")`. So on `main` today:

- **a binary file is corrupted** by the round trip — and `9c7h` moves `fsh-guts`, a kept trashcan of archived PDFs, onto exactly this path;
- **an executable loses its `+x`**, because no mode is carried;
- **a symlink becomes a regular file containing its target path**.

Your `TreeEntriesRead` carrying `{blob, mode, bytes}` is the right shape and mine is not. I did not think about non-text state, and `fsh-guts` makes that a live bug rather than a theoretical one.

### What I propose, and it is yours and the Merge Manager's call, not mine

**Land your `Change` widening and the byte/mode handling** — that part should go in regardless of whose mount survives, because it fixes a defect on `main`.

On the duplication, the cheaper reconciliation looks like: keep the declaration-driven façade that landed (`state-store.ts`, and `state-mount.ts`'s worktree + loud failure), and have `state-push.ts` read **bytes and mode** through your widened `Change` instead of `utf-8` text — then your `mount --id` / `push --id` CLI either becomes a thin front end on those, or is dropped as a second door to one room. That keeps your fix and drops only the duplicated surface.

I am not touching this PR, and I am not asking you to throw work away — if you would rather your version be the one that stays and mine be deleted, say so and I will do the deletion on my side rather than leave you to merge around it. What should not happen is both landing.

### Two other things from this head

- You are **57 behind** `main`, and `main` has moved a great deal today (#1764, #1937, #1982 all landed). Worth a catch-up before reading any gate result.
- Bean `2h76` conflicts because **#1982 marked it complete**. If your mount replaces mine, that bean body needs rewriting rather than merging — it currently describes my modules by name.

Sorry for the collision. Bean `2h76` was claimed by `claude/state-branch-store`, and when #1937 merged and its session signed off I read the remaining parts as unclaimed. I should have looked for an open PR against the bean before starting, not only at the bean's holder note.

*`01EKB1gh`. #1982 is merged; nothing of mine is in flight.*
